problem.text: Native Safetensors open failures previously raised only “Error opening file,” omitting both the filename and operating-system error.

reasoning.text: The patch captures errno immediately after a failed fopen and includes the filename, strerror description and numeric errno in TORCH_CHECK. Python adds a filename message before re-raising RuntimeError in both native loading branches.

impact.text: This improves failure diagnostics rather than repairing the underlying file-open failure: there is no retry, fallback or change to successful handle caching. Python header reading and the explicit python loading backend remain unchanged.

source_notes.text: Issue #33, “Error converting model,” reports a conversion traceback through get_tensor into stloader_open_file with the old generic error. Its relationship to this patch is inferred from that exact call and message match, plus a turboderp comment promising more informative diagnostics; the discussion does not establish the filesystem root cause.

Closed issue #17, “ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'torch' when installing requirements.txt,” concerns installation and Flash-Attention dependencies, not a reported Safetensors file-open failure.

limitations: No native extension, filesystem failure or CUDA path was executed. A scalar computation would not meaningfully validate errno propagation, thread synchronization or exception handling.
The underlying cause of the conversion failure reported in issue #33 remains unestablished.

claims.text: get_tensor resolves a tensor key to its filename and lazily opens native handles only when none are cached. The new Python guards cover both immediate mt_fread loading and deferred job creation; failed opens print the filename and propagate the exception without caching a result.

For immediate reads, worker error paths now copy errno into shared load_errnum, and the post-join check formats its description and number. CUDA copy failures still emit cudaGetErrorString separately. These changes add diagnostic information without changing chunk scheduling or transfer selection.

Deferred error reporting is asymmetric: the CPU worker captures errno but retains the generic post-join exception; the CUDA post-join exception gains errno formatting, but its worker never assigns load_errnum.

findings.description: The new deferred-CUDA diagnostic reports an initialized zero rather than the worker's error number.
findings.trigger: A read, seek or CUDA-copy failure reaches stloader_deferred_cuda's worker error label and subsequently reaches its post-join failure check.
findings.expected_behavior: The diagnostic should preserve the relevant failure information rather than present zero as the captured error number.
findings.actual_behavior: load_errnum is initialized to zero and never assigned in this function; the worker sets only load_failed, so the new exception formats strerror(0) and errno=0.

verification.description: Compared the complete parent function with the task diff. Whole-parent-tree literal caller search found the Python invocation in SafetensorsCollection.end_deferred_load and the native binding; the inspected caller passes CUDA workloads to this function. The observation therefore concerns deferred CUDA loads, not every get_tensor call.
verification.limits: No failure was induced; native exception propagation and runtime error text were not tested.

annotation.summary: Adds filename and errno diagnostics for native Safetensors open failures and expands read-error reporting, with an incomplete errno handoff in deferred CUDA loading.
